messages:
Linda: Heads-up — NimbusHealth reached out, saying after yesterday's model deploy their in-app assistant answers are "more prescriptive" and noticeably longer. They say product copy that used to be ~40 chars is now 70–90 chars and some responses add extra 'guidance' the UI didn't expect. They provided examples. Can someone triage?
Marco: Thanks — can you paste the sample request/response from the customer? Also which model ID did they mention?
Linda: Pasting customer repro (sanitized):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
{
  "model": "rwd-instruct-2026-03",
  "input": "Summarize the following appointment reminder for a patient in one sentence:",
  "context": "Your appointment is on Tue 3/16 at 3pm. Bring previous lab records.",
  "max_tokens": 60
}
```
Customer says prior to last-night deploy they got: 
"Appointment on Tue 3/16 at 3pm — bring prior lab records."
Now they get: 
"We recommend you come to your appointment on Tue 3/16 at 3pm and remember to bring your previous lab records; if you have any questions, call the clinic."
Linda: They call this "added guidance" and longer phrasing. It breaks a UI character limit.
Priya: Interesting — the model name looks like the new instruct-family we promoted last night. Noting this tag: rwd-instruct-2026-03. Deploy-bot shows a deploy at 1780230000 that updated that model variant to the default for the hosted inference path.
deploy-bot: deploy accepted — rwd-instruct-2026-03 promoted to stable, canary at 10% -> stable 100% (by platform policy) :rocket:
Ana: NimbusHealth flagged it as P1 for their UX flow. They're asking for either a quick mitigation or a configurable knob to limit 'advice-style elaboration' — they don't want us to change copy on their behalf.
Marco: Ok. First triage steps: 1) confirm delta between prior model and new model outputs on the same prompt distribution, 2) check whether temperature/top_p or system prompt injection changed in the default server-side preset, 3) see if any new postprocessing heuristics were added.
Priya: I'm running an automated diff across their provided prompt set now. Early result: median token count increased from 9 to 15 tokens for the sample set; the new model tends to append a polite suggestion sentence. No server-side postprocessing changes in the last deploy — confirmed via config history.
Priya: Attaching a minimal repro that shows the behavior difference for one prompt (sanitized):
```
# old model
> rwd-chat-2026-02
Output: "Appointment on Tue 3/16 at 3pm — bring prior lab records."

# new model
> rwd-instruct-2026-03
Output: "We recommend you come to your appointment on Tue 3/16 at 3pm and remember to bring your previous lab records; if you have any questions, call the clinic."
```
Marco: Thanks. That suggests a change in model style rather than system prompts. Two immediate mitigations: 1) flip NimbusHealth's routed model back to the previous model variant for their org (quick, per-customer routing), or 2) apply a stricter max_tokens or a shortness prompt wrapper on their requests. Which do they prefer?
Linda: NimbusHealth prefers us to revert on our side for now; product team worried the shortness prompt wrapper could leak into other places. They asked for rollback to previous variant for their API key.
Ana: I'll coordinate with account to get permission for a per-org rollback. They want messaging that we "investigate the stylistic change" — no promises about product text.
Priya: I can set up per-key routing to rwd-chat-2026-02 for NimbusHealth within 15 minutes. Will also run a quick eval across their top 50 prompts to quantify regression.
Marco: After that, let's produce a short RCA: did the new instruct model intentionally shift default response style? Was there a training/objective tweak or a prompt-template update? Priya, loop in Research if needed.
Priya: Noted. Early logs: no server side prompt template change. Reaching out to model-onboarding team to see what changed in the instruct family training/objective or post-train calibrations.
Linda: NimbusHealth — going to route you back to the previous model variant for your API key while we investigate. ETA ~20min.
Marco: Also keep an eye on latency — switching variants might change tail latency numbers for that org. I'll watch the per-key metrics.
Priya: Quick update: per-key routing done for their key -> rwd-chat-2026-02. Customer confirms reduced verbosity in a test.
NimbusHealth (quoted): "Thanks — that's closer to what we expect. Please let us know findings."
Linda: I'll confirm SLOs/impact, then prepare a short customer-facing note and internal ticket.
Marco: For the RCA, candidate causes to investigate: objective function tweak (e.g., added instruction-following loss that encourages elaboration), dataset mixture shift, or temperature default change during model packaging. Also check for any default safety/softening layers that insert 'helpful' guidance.
Priya: Reached out to model-onboard and research. Research responded: there was a packaging change to the instruct family that added a short 'assistant-suggest' bias to encourage advice when prompts looked like reminders. This was meant to improve helpfulness on consumer assistants but has UX regressions for terse enterprise flows. They're preparing a patch to make that bias configurable and to decouple it from the stable tag.
Ana: Good find. Next steps for action items: 1) keep per-key routing for NimbusHealth until we ship a configurable flag, 2) research to publish a short note in the release channel about the change and mitigation knobs, 3) support to send a reconciled message to NimbusHealth with ETA.
Marco: I'm filing an internal incident ticket and assigning to Priya + research. Linda, can you draft the customer note? Keep it factual: we reverted routing and are investigating why the new instruct packaging encouraged longer 'guidance' sentences. No language about "we broke the model" — focus on style fit and upcoming configurable control.
Linda: Drafting now. Will send to Ana for tone review.
Priya: I'll follow up with a quantitative delta and attach diff examples in the ticket.
deploy-bot: incident created — ticket #INC-2026-4789 (priorty P1)
Ana: NimbusHealth responded to the revert: "Appreciate the quick action. We'll test more and send examples if anything else pops up." :thumbsup:
Marco: OK — keep monitoring. If more customers report similar regressions, we need to add a checklist item to model promotion verifying 'brevity impact' on enterprise prompt templates.
Linda: Thanks team. Closing loop once RCA lands.
